newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair hit by budget house tax.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair hit by budget house tax.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair was one of the first victims of the budget unveiled on Wednesday by Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer, Gordon Brown.
Brown announced he was immediately increasing a tax on home purchases to prevent already soaring prices overheating.
Brown said the stamp duty tax would be doubled from one to two percent on houses worth more than 500,000 pounds ($828,400).
Blair, who said last month he was selling his family home in the fashionable London district of Islington because of security considerations, grinned sheepishly as Brown announced the move.

Blair, his lawyer wife Cherie and their three children have moved into an official flat in Downing Street, although they broke with tradition by moving into number 11 rather than the cramped lodgings over the prime minister's office at number 10.

Estate agents expect Blair to get at least 615,000 pounds for his five-bedroom house. This means a tidy profit for the Blairs, who bought the house for 375,000 pounds five years ago. But it now also means more income for the new Labour government.
